summary.text: Deborah Glick has represented Lower Manhattan in the Assembly for more than 30 years and chairs the Assembly Committee on Environmental Conservation.
Her official biography says she was the first openly LGBTQ member of the state legislature and the lead sponsor of the Reproductive Health Act.

paragraphs.text: Glick was born and raised in Queens and has lived in Greenwich Village for over 40 years, according to her Assembly biography.
She holds a bachelor's degree from Queens College and a Master of Business Administration from Fordham University.

The biography lists her legislative work as including the Reproductive Health Act, a bill requiring courts to consider a companion animal's best interest in divorce custody, renewal of the Loft Law, and a bill expanding New York City's school-zone speed safety camera program.

It says she led the fight for marriage equality and was primary sponsor of a ban on conversion therapy and of the Hospital Visitation Act, and that she fought to pass the Sexual Orientation Non-Discrimination Act and the Gender Expression Non-Discrimination Act.
Besides chairing Environmental Conservation, she serves on the Ways and Means, Rules and Governmental Operations Committees.
